structures.name: Pectoralis major muscle
objects: Clavicular head of pectoralis major muscle.r
Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle.r

rows: Clavicular head: medial half of the clavicle. Sternocostal head: sternum, upper six costal cartilages, and the aponeurosis of the external oblique.
Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
Lateral and medial pectoral nerves (C5 to T1).
Adducts and medially rotates the arm. The clavicular head flexes the arm. The sternocostal head extends it from a flexed position.

structures.name: Deltoid muscle
objects: Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle.r

rows: Lateral third of the clavicle, the acromion, and the spine of the scapula.
The main abductor of the arm, working with supraspinatus, which starts the movement. The anterior fibers flex and medially rotate the arm. The posterior fibers extend and laterally rotate it.
hy: The axillary nerve is injured by a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus or an anterior dislocation of the shoulder: the deltoid flattens, abduction is weak, and sensation is lost over the lateral shoulder.

rows: Short head: tip of the coracoid process. Long head: supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula.
Radial tuberosity and, through the bicipital aponeurosis, the deep fascia of the forearm.
Supinates the forearm, most strongly with the elbow flexed, and flexes the elbow.
hy: The biceps reflex tests C5 and C6.

rows: Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus.
Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna.
Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6). A small lateral part is supplied by the radial nerve.
Flexes the elbow in every position of the forearm.

Aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle, at the upper end of the anterior layer of the rectus sheath. It is the lowest and smallest of the three heads of pectoralis major, below the clavicular and sternocostal heads, and many texts count it as part of the sternocostal head.

Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus, by the common tendon of pectoralis major. Its fibers pass upward behind those of the other heads, so the lowest fibers of the muscle attach highest on the humerus.
Mainly the medial pectoral nerve (C8, T1), which supplies the lower fibers of pectoralis major.
Adducts and medially rotates the arm with the rest of the muscle. With the lower sternocostal fibers it pulls a raised arm down toward the trunk and helps to draw the shoulder down.
